metadata.title: Chapter 5: Verbs and Actions (क्रिया - Kriya)
metadata.subject: Hindi
learning_outcomes: Understand what verbs (क्रिया) are in the Hindi language
Identify action words in sentences and everyday conversation
Differentiate between root verbs (धातु) and complete verbs (क्रिया)
Recognize how actions change based on gender and number

ai_context.learning_goal: Master the identification and usage of action words (verbs) in Hindi, connecting daily physical actions to grammatical structures.
common_misconceptions: Confusing nouns (संज्ञा) with verbs (क्रिया) because both can be subjects of thought.
Thinking all words ending in 'ना' are always verbs without looking at the action context.

blocks.title: The Silent World Mystery
blocks.body: Imagine waking up in a world where everything has stopped. You try to speak, but no sound comes out. You try to run, but your legs are frozen like statues. There is no walking, no eating, no laughing, and no playing. How boring would that be? Every single day, from the moment we open our eyes to the moment we fall asleep, our body and mind are constantly moving and doing things. In grammar, these doing words are the magical heartbeat of every sentence. Without them, sentences are just lifeless ghosts. Welcome to the wonderful world of actions!

blocks.question: Based on our opening story, what makes a sentence come alive?
options: Just the names of people and places
Doing words that show movement and action
blocks.explanation: Doing words (actions) give life and movement to a sentence, telling us what is actually happening.

blocks.title: Concept 1: What is a [DICT_HINDI_KRIYA|Verb]?
blocks.body: In the Hindi language, words that tell us about an action being done or happening are called [DICT_HINDI_KRIYA|क्रिया] (Kriya), which translates to verbs. Whether you are drinking water (पीना), reading a book (पढ़ना), running in the park (दौड़ना), or sleeping in your bed (सोना), every single movement is a verb. Think of verbs as the engine of a train. The nouns are the bogies, but the verb is what pulls the entire sentence forward down the track. Whenever you ask yourself 'What is someone doing?', the answer you get is always a verb.

blocks.title: Flashcard: Verb (क्रिया)
blocks.body:
Front: What do we call words that show actions like खाना (eating) or पढ़ना (reading)? 
Back: They are called क्रिया (Kriya) or Verbs!

blocks.title: The Classroom Charades Challenge
blocks.body: Stand up and act out brushing your teeth without speaking. Ask a friend to guess the Hindi word for it (ब्रश करना / दाuten साफ करना). This physical connection makes grammar stick forever in your memory!

blocks.title: Concept 2: Recognizing [DICT_HINDI_KAAM|Action Words] in Daily Life
blocks.body: Actions are happening all around us, all the time. When mother cooks food in the kitchen, 'cooks' ([DICT_HINDI_KAAM|पकाना]) is the action. When birds fly in the sky, 'fly' ([DICT_HINDI_KAAM|उड़ना]) is the action. In Hindi grammar, action words are categorized based on whether someone is doing them consciously or whether they are happening naturally, like rain falling (बरसना) or flowers blooming (खिलना). Let's look closely at a sentence: 'रोहन गेंद खेल रहा है' (Rohan is playing with a ball). Here, 'खेल रहा है' tells us the exact activity Rohan is engaged in.

blocks.question: In the sentence 'सीता किताब पढ़ रही है' (Sita is reading a book), which word is the action word (क्रिया)?
blocks.explanation: 'पढ़ रही है' (Reading) is the action being performed by Sita.

blocks.title: Concept 3: The Root of Verbs - [DICT_HINDI_DHATU|Dhatu]
blocks.body: Every Hindi verb has a core root from which it is born. This root is called [DICT_HINDI_DHATU|धातु] (Dhatu). For example, the root 'पड़' (pad) is the seed. When we add 'ना' (na) to it, it becomes the full verb 'पढ़ना' (to read). Similarly, 'लिख' (likh) becomes 'लिखना' (to write), and 'चल' (chal) becomes 'चलना' (to walk). Understanding the Dhatu helps you understand how verbs are built from simple building blocks. It is like learning the root of a plant before looking at its leaves and flowers.

blocks.title: Flashcard: Dhatu (धातु)
blocks.body:
Front: What is the root form of the verb 'खाना' (to eat)? 
Back: The root Dhatu is 'खा' (kha).

blocks.question: If the verb is 'दौड़ना' (to run), what is its root Dhatu?
blocks.explanation: 'दौड़' is the root part (Dhatu) to which 'ना' is added to form the complete verb.

blocks.title: Concept 4: Actions Can Happen Inside or Outside
blocks.body: Not all actions involve running, jumping, or physical body movement that you can see with your eyes. Some actions happen quietly inside our minds or bodies. When you think ([DICT_HINDI_KRIYA|सोचना]), dream ([DICT_HINDI_KRIYA|सपना देखना]), feel happy ([DICT_HINDI_KRIYA|खुश होना]), or cry ([DICT_HINDI_KRIYA|रोना]), these are also classified as verbs. Even 'to be' words like 'है' (is), 'था' (was), and 'होगा' (will be) act as linking verbs that connect subjects to their states of being.

blocks.title: Mind Detective Game
blocks.body: Close your eyes for 10 seconds. Think about what you will eat for dinner. Open your eyes and name the mental action you just did ('सोचना' or 'विचार करना'). Mental actions count as verbs too!

blocks.question: Which of the following is an internal/mental action classified as a verb?
blocks.explanation: 'सोचना' (To think) is a mental action, making it a valid verb.

blocks.title: Concept 5: How Verbs Change with Gender (लिंग)
blocks.body: In Hindi, verbs have a special superpower: they change their clothes (forms) based on who is doing the action! If a boy is running, we say 'लड़का दौड़ रहा है'. But if a girl is running, the verb changes to 'लड़की दौड़ रही है'. Notice how 'रहा है' changed to 'रही है' just because the subject shifted from male to female. This agreement between the subject's gender and the verb is one of the most important rules in Hindi grammar.

blocks.title: Flashcard: Gender Agreement
blocks.body:
Front: Complete the sentence for a girl: 'वह खाना खा ___ है' (She is eating food). 
Back: रही (rahi) -> 'वह खाना खा रही है'.

blocks.question: Choose the correct verb form for a boy eating: 'बालक सेब खा ___ है।'
blocks.explanation: Since 'बालक' (boy) is masculine singular, the correct auxiliary verb form is 'रहा'.

blocks.title: Concept 6: Singular and Plural Verbs (वचन)
blocks.body: Just like verbs change for gender, they also change when the number of people changes from one to many (singular to plural). If one child is playing, we say 'बच्चा खेल रहा है'. But if multiple children are playing, the verb becomes plural: 'बच्चे खेल रहे हैं'. Notice how 'रहा है' turned into 'रहे हैं'. Verbs always match the team size of the subject!

blocks.title: Plural Powerup
blocks.body: Write down 'घोड़ा दौड़ रहा है' on a paper. Now cross it out and rewrite it for many horses. Watch how both the noun (घोड़ा -> घोड़े) and the verb (रहा है -> रहे हैं) transform together like dance partners.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank for plural: 'पक्षी आकाश में उड़ ___ हैं।'
blocks.explanation: 'पक्षी' (birds) is plural, so we use 'रहे हैं'.

blocks.title: Concept 7: Action Categories - Transitive and Intransitive Preview
blocks.body: As you grow more advanced in Hindi, you will notice that some actions need an object to make complete sense, while others do not. For example, if someone says 'राम ने खाया' (Ram ate), you naturally want to ask 'What did he eat?'. Here, 'खाना' is a transitive action needing an object like 'आम' (mango). On the other hand, if someone says 'पक्ष़ी उड़ते हैं' (Birds fly), you don't need to ask 'what'—flying is complete by itself. This distinction makes Hindi sentence structure wonderfully precise.

blocks.title: Flashcard: Action Completion
blocks.body:
Front: Does the action 'सोना' (to sleep) need an object like a ball or book to make sense? 
Back: No! You just sleep; it's a complete standalone action.

blocks.question: Which sentence has an action that directly targets an object?
options: बच्चा हँस रहा है (The child is laughing)
मोहित पुस्तक पढ़ रहा है (Mohit is reading a book)
पक्षी उड़ रहे हैं (Birds are flying)
blocks.explanation: 'पुस्तक पढ़ रहा है' has the object 'पुस्तक' (book) receiving the action of reading.

blocks.title: Concept 8: Finding Verbs in a Story
blocks.body: Let's read a mini story and hunt for verbs: 'एक शेर जंगल में सो रहा था। एक चूहा आया और कूदने लगा। शेर जाग गया।' (A lion was sleeping in the forest. A mouse came and began to jump. The lion woke up.) Here, our action words are: सो रहा था (was sleeping), आया (came), कूदने लगा (began to jump), and जाग गया (woke up). Without these action verbs, we would just have a random list of animals with no plot!

blocks.title: Storybook Safari
blocks.body: Open any Hindi storybook, grab a yellow crayon, and highlight every single action word you find on page one. You will be amazed to see how colorful your page becomes!

blocks.question: In the phrase 'शेर जाग गया' (The lion woke up), what is the main action?
blocks.explanation: 'जाग गया' describes the change of state and action of the lion waking up.

blocks.title: Summary: Master Checklist for Hindi Verbs
blocks.body: Let's review our journey through Chapter 5. 1. Verbs (क्रिया) are doing words that show physical or mental actions. 2. Every verb comes from a root called Dhatu (धातु) like 'पढ़' or 'खा'. 3. Verbs adapt like chameleons, changing their endings based on whether the subject is masculine or feminine, singular or plural. By keeping these rules in mind, your Hindi writing and speaking will become clear, powerful, and alive!

blocks.question: What is the primary purpose of a verb (क्रिया) in any sentence?
options: To tell us what action is taking place
To describe the color of an object
To state the name of a city
blocks.explanation: Verbs exist specifically to express actions, occurrences, or states of being.
